proposed_results: For every fixed d >= 2, A_d(n) = Theta_d(n^d (log n)^(d-1)), where A_d(n) = sum(j=1..n) C_d(j).
For every fixed d >= 4, C_d(n) = Omega_d(n^(d-1) (log n)^(d-2)).
reason_for_investigation: If valid and not already established, the second statement increases the lower logarithmic exponent in the inspected corner-cut baseline. The first identifies the sharp three-dimensional upper exponent on average.
proof_mechanism: Uniform dimension induction for primitive simplices in separated axis boxes, with a finite explicit error bound before taking limits.
Primitive maximal minors give the full parallel integer-lattice basis, making the selected simplex recoverable from its plane.
Distinct planes give distinct interior arrangement vertices; chamber count dominates interior vertices in a convex parameter domain.
Geometrically separated axis-extent ranges prevent duplication across Theta_d((log n)^(d-1)) aspect choices.
The published lifting lemma converts the cumulative result to an exact-size lower bound with logarithmic exponent d-2 for every fixed d >= 4.

finite_evidence.limitations: Finite evidence does not prove the density asymptotics, the full argument or novelty.
finite_evidence.negative_control: Without a primitive projected frame, changing the last coordinate can leave every tested value bad modulo 2; the one-residue bound fails.

checked_steps: Conditioning uses the joint projected events and preserves all next-step free coordinates.
The controlling determinant is nonzero for every allowed projected configuration.
Primitive projected rank at every prime gives exactly one bad residue for the last coordinate.
Large bad primes divide one fixed nonzero determinant; no infinite-union density interchange.
The all-dimensional closed threshold follows from elementary monotone exponential inequalities.
A primitive frame is the full parallel integer-lattice basis; scaled inverse bounds give injectivity.
Interior-vertex/chamber inequality holds for arbitrary degeneracies in an open convex domain.
Observable axis extents prevent duplicate cuts across scale tuples.
Explicit cardinality, composition, floor and constant calculations give the claimed uniform lower bound.
Lifting improves the exact-size lower exponent only in d>=4; the d=3 exact-size gap remains.
